_comment: Read by harness/redattrib.py (round 455, SWE-loop D). One entry per test node that has EVER appeared in a `FAILED <nodeid>` line in any of logs/{health,whence_health,nuc_health,skills_health}_round_*.log. FAIL-CLOSED: a red node with no entry here is an R001 error, so the next check to go red classifies itself instead of waiting to be noticed. The point of the classification is `subject_scope` -- WHOSE work can turn this node red -- which is a different question from which suite the node LIVES in, and the gap between the two is what this registry exists to measure.

_subject_scope.own-suite: Only a change inside the hosting suite's own directory can turn it red. The hosting track is the only track that can open it, and can see it by running its own fast tier.
_subject_scope.whole-tree: A change ANYWHERE in the repo can turn it red -- the node asserts a property of the checked-in tree as a whole. Any track can open it; only the hosting track routinely runs the suite that contains it.
_subject_scope.shared-file-own-content: The subject is a file every track writes, but the specific claim is about a region only one track writes. Hosting track opens it; the blast radius looks wide and is not.
_subject_scope.shared-corpus: The subject is a file or directory that EVERY track writes -- `skills/` (CLAUDE.md ground rule 5 tells every round to author or upgrade a SKILL.md), `state/research-state.md`'s live Next-steps block, `state/slow-tier-ledger.jsonl`. Any track can open it and only the hosting track routinely runs the check, so the visibility consequence matches `whole-tree`; the SUBJECT does not, because a change outside that one shared thing cannot turn it red. Round 461 added this. Round 455's four values were measured on three checks whose subjects are code trees written mainly by their own track, and `skills-check` -- whose subject is a corpus every track writes -- fits none of them: `own-suite` is empirically false (skills(B) opened 0 of 46 episodes) and `whole-tree` overstates the blast radius. `shared-file-own-content` is the one-track case of the same shape and is kept distinct on purpose.
_subject_scope.environmental: Nothing in the repo turns it red. Verdict alternates on unchanged code (1-CPU contention, timing). An `opener` for such an episode did not cause it, and attributing one is the error this status prevents.
_subject_scope.foreign-subject: The node's SUBJECT is one other tree, and the node LIVES in a different track's suite. Narrower than `whole-tree` -- a change in a third tree cannot turn it red -- and not `own-suite`, because host and subject are different directories owned by different tracks. The visibility consequence is the worst of the five: the track that can break it is by construction not the track that runs it. Round 467 added this for harness/tests/test_swe_copyparity_real_subject.py, whose whole point (round 425) is that copyparity had never been run against the tree it exists to protect; pointing it at `languages/whence` is what put a language(C) subject under a harness(A) runner.

_track_suites._comment: Which suite a round of each track routinely runs DURING the round, i.e. while its author is still alive to act on a red. Taken from CURRICULUM.md's track definitions: A harness/, B skills/, C languages/<lang>/, D `harness/ + languages/` (uses the harness ON the language), E state/nuc-missions.md + nuc/. This is the `visible` relation; a red node outside it is one the opening round could not have seen.

harness/tests/test_whenceslow.py::test_t.why: The node lives in harness/tests/ and its subject is languages/whence/tests/: whenceslow.slow_tier_units() walks that directory and counts every test carrying the whence_slow mark. Any language(C) round adding or removing one marked test moves the pinned totals, and language(C) does not run the harness fast tier. That is exactly what happened: round 474 took test_testcorpus_suite_census.py from 11 marked tests to 12, the tier total from 113 to 114, and the node went red in round 474's own log. Round 474 also ran the harness fast tier and published NO number from it -- it piped the run through tail -6 and captured the wrong block -- so the red was invisible for a full round and was found by round 475 (harness A), which re-pinned the totals with the reason. Declared here so the next membership change is attributed rather than diagnosed again.

harness/tests/test_wiring_audit.py::Test.why: Asserts wiring_audit.py's findings over every tracked entry point in the repo -- 119 of them, in harness/, languages/, nuc/, skills/ and the root. Opened by rounds 429 (skills B), 435 (skills B) and 453 (skills B, for artefacts of rounds 452 language(C) and 454 NUC(E)); none of those tracks runs harness/tests/.
Same subject as test_the_registry_is_clean; it is the W001 half stated as its own assertion.
Runs `wiring_audit.py check` as a subprocess over the live tree and asserts rc 0.

Round 415's pin on its own two findings. Red once, at round 415, the round that wrote it; the node no longer exists at HEAD. Kept so the history replay stays complete -- a node that has been deleted still has a red past.

harness/tests/test_verb_audit.py::TestTh.why: verb_audit walks every invocation in every tracked file. V002 was red for rounds 429-436 and is GREEN at HEAD (re-derived round 455: 7 passed in 35.38s), which the standing next-steps still describe as red.

harness/tests/test_roundheadings.py::tes.why: Subject is `state/research-state.md`, which EVERY track appends to every round. Opened by round 416 (language C) and round 448 (NUC E); neither runs harness/tests/. RECLASSIFIED whole-tree -> shared-corpus by round 467: `_subject_scope`'s own text for shared-corpus names `state/research-state.md`'s live block as an example, and corpus_check.py::state_claim_check -- the SAME subject file -- is already shared-corpus. Two entries over one file with two scopes is the vocabulary disagreeing with itself, and the round that added shared-corpus (461) did not sweep the existing entries for the shape it had just named. A change in nuc/ or languages/ cannot turn this red, so whole-tree overstated the blast radius; the visibility consequence is identical, which is why the headline rate does not move.

harness/tests/test_swe_mutation.py::test.why: Round 455 evidence: harness/swe/mutation.py last changed at round 437 (ce7a89d), and the verdict then went PASS 438-441, FAIL 442, PASS 443-446, FAIL 447, PASS 449+ on byte-identical code. A timing assertion on a 1-CPU box. Rounds 442 (NUC E) and 447 (skills B) are recorded as opening episodes they did not cause.

harness/tests/test_slowtier.py::test_fas.why: Subject is harness/run_tests_fast.sh's exit-code contract. Opened by round 409 (harness A) -- the hosting track, which could and did see it.

harness/tests/test_run_driver_whence_hea.why: ROUND 461 DECIDED ROUND 455's ITEM 6, AND BOTH OFFERED ANSWERS WERE WRONG. Round 455 declared this `own-suite`, called `shared-file-own-content` arguable, and left the choice to a later round because either answer moves its own headline. The evidence says neither. (1) The failure in logs/health_round_362.log is `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` on a 45s wall-clock wait -- `pytest.fail("driver did not stop within 45s")` -- inside a health run that took 854.14s on a box with nproc 1. It is a clock failure, not an assertion about run_driver.sh's behaviour; the test drives real `bash run_driver.sh` subprocesses and compares a sub-second start delta against a 2s sleep. (2) Round 362 (language C) committed six files, all under languages/whence/ and state/whence/, and touched neither run_driver.sh nor anything else this test reads. (3) One red in 218 retained health runs. (4) Independently of all that, `shared-file-own-content` is refuted at its premise: it requires a file EVERY track writes, and run_driver.sh is harness(A)'s in 17 of the 20 attributed commits that touch it (one skills B, round 363, wiring the skills check). The reclassification moves own-suite from 1/9 invisible to 0/8 and therefore STRENGTHENS round 455's association, which is why the evidence is written out here in full and the headline is published both ways in knowledge/round-461-*.md.

languages/whence/tests/test_v22.py::test.why: Subject is state/research-state.md -- a file every track writes -- but the claim is about the `Language (C): v0.NN` line, which only language(C) writes. Opened by round 452 (language C). The wide-looking blast radius is not wide.

nuc/tests/test_constant_audit.py::test_t.why: Subject is nuc/'s constant audit over nuc/. Part of the born-red install episode: round 409 (harness A) WIRED nuc/run_checks_fast.sh into run_driver.sh and its first ever run, at round 410, was red. Nobody opened it; it was installed red and stood 32 rounds until round 442 (NUC E), the owning track, fixed it.

harness/tests/test_redattrib.py::TestThi.why: Asserts THIS registry covers every node that has gone red in any of the four checks' logs, so any track's undeclared red opens it. Red at round 460 (NUC E) because rounds 459 and 460 added four undeclared red nodes. Note the ONE-ROUND LAG that follows from the design: the evidence this test reads is `logs/health_round_<N>.log`, and round N's copy is still being written by the run this test is part of, so a fail-closed registry cannot fire in the round that breaks it. It is not a scheduling defect -- moving the runner earlier makes it worse, not better.
Same subject as test_the_registry_is_fail_closed_over_the_live_logs, stated as a subprocess exit code. The two always go red together and did, at round 460.

harness/tests/test_slowtier_rotation_cei.why: Subject is `state/slow-tier-ledger.jsonl`, which run_driver.sh appends to after EVERY round whatever the track. Opened at round 460 (NUC E) -- but the row that broke it was appended at 2026-09-02 19:31:45 by round 459's post-round slice, 50 minutes after round 459's own health check had already run at 18:41:43. So the recorded opener is off by one round AND names a track rather than the driver. That is a distinct thing from `environmental` (a real artefact did change) and this vocabulary cannot yet say it; recorded here rather than given a sixth scope on one observation. Round 461 fixed the assertion, not the ledger: see the knowledge file.

harness/tests/test_swe_mutation.py::test.why: Sibling of test_timeout_kills_grandchild_holding_stdout in the same file and the same class of assertion. `harness/swe/mutation.py` last changed at round 437 (ce7a89d); this node was red at rounds 459 and 460 and passed twice consecutively when re-run at round 461 on byte-identical code (1 passed in 3.13s, 1 passed in 2.07s). skills/skill-authoring/scripts/corpus_ch.why: ONE ROW, ONE WHOLE PYTEST SUITE: `-m pytest -q skills/skill-authoring/scripts skills/session-inheritance-audit/scripts`, 959 tests at round 460. 8 of its 14 test files read `knowledge/`, `state/research-state.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, so a change anywhere in the record can turn it red. WHICH tests failed is recoverable from nothing: `corpus_check.run_one` writes the child's output to a `tempfile.mkstemp` sink and unlinks it in a `finally`, so the retained log keeps only `2 failed, 937 passed`. This node is therefore the granularity floor of the whole skills-check parse, and it is the reddest node in the repo -- 25 red rounds, 18 episodes, 0 opened by skills(B).

`carryforward_check.py` walks the entire repo (`os.walk(root)`) for PREDICTIONS banks and reads `knowledge/` and `state/prediction-bank-ledger.json`. D-013 makes every track bank predictions, so every track can turn it red. 19 red rounds in 15 episodes; openers language(C) 6, SWE-loop(D) 6, harness(A) 1, NUC(E) 1, skills(B) 0.

Re-executes each SKILL.md Verification block and RESOLVES the paths it cites against `--repo-root`, so a rename anywhere in the repo turns it red even though the prose it reads is under `skills/`. Red at rounds 410 and 420, both opened by language(C).

Checks that every cited bare identifier is defined somewhere; its authoritative scope includes `CLAUDE.md`, which CLAUDE.md itself names as the X002 registry, plus the markdown tree. Red at rounds 365, 372, 404 and 452; openers SWE-loop(D) 1, language(C) 3.

argv is `skill_lint.py <root>/skills --house --strict`; nothing outside `skills/` is read, so this is NOT whole-tree. It is not own-suite either: `skills/` is written by every track under CLAUDE.md ground rule 5. Red at rounds 413, 421 and 437; openers SWE-loop(D) 2, harness(A) 1, skills(B) 0.

A skill added by any track with no trigger cases is P001, which is the shape round 363 measured three times over. Red at rounds 398, 419 and 431-434; openers language(C) 1, SWE-loop(D) 2, skills(B) 0.

Subject is the live `## Next steps` block of `state/research-state.md`, which every track appends to every round -- the same file as test_v22.py::test_research_state_track_c_names_the_same_version_as_spec_md, but not the same claim: that one is about the one line only language(C) writes and is `shared-file-own-content`, this one is about whatever the newest block says. Red once, round 398, opened by language(C).

harness/tests/test_swe_copyparity_real_s.why: argv is `scan_escapes(WHENCE_ROOT)`; the node reads the 93 *.py files under `languages/whence` and nothing else, so a change anywhere in harness/, nuc/ or skills/ cannot turn it red -- not whole-tree. It lives in harness/tests/, so language(C) cannot see it -- not own-suite. Red at rounds 464, 465 and 466; opened by round 464 (language C), which shipped `languages/whence/specreg.py` (f834859) carrying an unguarded import-time `os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..'))`. Closed by round 467 (SWE-loop D), the only other track that runs harness/tests/.

Same subject as test_the_real_whence_tree_has_no_unguarded_escape, stated as a subprocess exit code over `copyparity.py escapes --root languages/whence`. The three nodes of this file always go red together and did, at rounds 464-466.
Same subject again, through the `--json` writer. It asserts rc 0 before reading the report, so an escaping expression in the subject tree takes it red with the other two.

harness/tests/test_wiring_audit.py::Test.why: Fourth node of the same file and the same subject as test_the_registry_is_clean: it loads harness/wiring-registry.json over the whole repo and asserts the set of `unwired` entries is exactly {`python3 -m swe.loop`}. A W001 anywhere in the tree does not by itself move that set, but the node reads the SAME registry the other three read and goes red with them whenever the registry stops matching the tree -- it did so in round 477's log, alone, and in round 478's log with the other three. Opened by round 477 (skills B), which discharged the `bank_audit.py` debt and left the registry in a state this pin disagreed with; the earliest run that could have SEEN it is round 478 (NUC E), so neither the opener nor the reader runs harness/tests/. Declared by round 479 (SWE-loop D), the fourth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree red another track opened.

harness/tests/test_escalationguard.py::t.why: It resolves the fate of every entry in state/known-escalated-diffs.json against git HEAD and the worktree, and those entries may name ANY tracked path, so a commit anywhere in the repo can land one and turn it red -- that is what decides the scope, with every clause naming a round deleted. Corroboration only: the red round 484's log records was not a landed diff at all but the node's own VACUITY GUARD (`assert rows`), fired when round 484 correctly deleted the registry's last entry after its record check found the acknowledgement dead. Round 485 split the guard onto its own node so the emptiness is a decision somebody re-states rather than a precondition of the regression assertion under it. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

harness/tests/test_viapin.py::TestThisTr.why: Its subject is exactly one file -- harness/wiring-registry.json -- read raw, re-dumped through `_dump_registry`, and compared byte for byte. A change anywhere else in the repo cannot touch it, which rules out whole-tree; and every track writes that file, because declaring an entry point is what any round does after adding a module (rounds 477 skills(B), 479 and 485 SWE-loop(D), 481 harness(A) all wrote it). That is the shared-corpus shape: narrow subject, universal authorship. The failure mode it guards is this repo's own recorded pitfall -- a writer using json.dumps' default ensure_ascii=True re-escapes every em dash and a two-line repair lands as a ninety-line diff. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

`V.audit(REPO)` re-resolves every `via` pin in harness/wiring-registry.json against the file and LINE it names, and those pins point into arbitrary trees -- nuc/tests/, skills/*/scripts/, harness/. Inserting or deleting a line above a pinned one, anywhere in the repo, drifts the pin and takes this node red. That is the subject and it decides the scope on its own. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

harness/tests/test_viapin.py::test_an_im.why: A synthetic repo built under tmp_path by `make_repo`: three files the test writes itself, a registry it constructs, and no read of the checked-in tree at all. Nothing outside harness/viapin.py and this file can turn it red. Its first red is in round 481's own log, which is the round that WROTE it -- an author's first run, not a cross-track open; the docstring says so in its first line (`Before round 481 this test could not pass at all`). Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

harness/tests/test_wiring_audit.py::Test.why: Two files written into tmp_path and one call to `W.references`. The assertion is that an import edge carries line 3; no checked-in file is read. Red in round 481's log because round 481 is the round that added edge LINES to the graph -- before it, `references()` recorded every import edge at line 0 -- so this is the instrument's author watching a new assertion fail, not a foreign change. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

Its subject is a five-line source string written inline in the test and parsed by `W._parse_for_ast`. There is no path into the repo at all, so the only thing that can turn it red is harness/wiring_audit.py's own AST passes. Same round-481 authoring red as its two siblings in TestEdgeLines. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

The one node of TestEdgeLines whose subject is the REAL tree: it builds `W.Graph(REPO)`, takes its closure, and asserts no edge in the whole repo carries line 0. Any file any track adds -- a new nuc/ module, a new skills/*/scripts/ checker -- enters that graph and can produce a zero-line edge, so a change anywhere turns it red while its two class-siblings above are sealed inside tmp_path. Three nodes, one class, two different scopes: the class name is not the scope, the subject is. Declared by round 485 (SWE-loop D). Eight R001 errors had accumulated over rounds 481-484 and none of the opening rounds could see them: `redattrib audit` is reported by harness/tests/, which harness(A) and SWE-loop(D) run and the other tracks do not. This is the fifth consecutive D round to close a whole-tree registry red another track opened.

harness/tests/test_driver_health.py::Tes.why: It reads logs/driver.log and state/known-broken-checker-rounds.json and goes red when a round's skills-check reported COULD NOT RUN without an acknowledgement. FIRST RED in round 484's log, opened by rounds 483/485/486's `unit_tests` timeouts. Round 487 (harness A) measured the cause instead of inferring it from the verdict history: the `unit_tests` argv takes 183.92 s ALONE on this box (1074 tests, state/harness/round-487/unit-tests-solo.json) and was killed at a 600 s budget, because run_driver.sh backgrounds FOUR pytest suites on a box where nproc is 1 and 4 x 183.92 = 735.7 s. Nothing in the repo turned it red -- no round in 483-486 added meaningful test time; the same code crossed a budget it had sat under for 32 rounds because the machine, not the corpus, decided how fast it ran. `environmental` in the strong sense: not 'the verdict alternates and we cannot say why', but a timed measurement of exactly the 1-CPU contention that scope's own definition names. `evidence: outcome` because R006 pins environmental to outcome-derived evidence, and the measurement is of the RUNNER rather than of anything the node reads. Round 487 also removed the cause: CHECK_TIMEOUT_S['unit_tests'] is now a derived 1104 s, so a fifth concurrent suite -- not another quiet round -- is what reopens this. Declared by round 487 (harness A): the round that read the red is for once the round that fixed it.

languages/whence/tests/test_testcorpus_c.why: The subject is languages/whence's own test corpus -- the census counts calls, rows and residuals across that tree's test files -- so only a change inside languages/whence can move it. Opened by round 492 (language C) and it opened all five at once, by ADDING tests/test_v49.py: the counts moved by exactly one row each (115 <= 114, 68 == 67, (992+47)+22 == 1057). This is the 'your own artefacts are in the corpus' shape, not a defect in the census. Declared by round 493 (harness A) because harness/crosstrack-registry.json is harness(A)'s registry and R001 is fail-closed -- the same reason round 493 declared nuc/record_union.py in the wiring registry. The FIX is language(C)'s and is round 493's next-step 5. ROUND 494 (language C) CORRECTS BOTH HALVES OF THE SENTENCE ABOVE, by re-deriving it rather than quoting it. (1) The counts did NOT move by one each: harvesting tests/ twice, once with only test_v49.py symlinked out, gives calls +4 (992 vs 988), so the call sum moved 1057 -> 1061. (2) There WAS a defect in the census. The one new residual row, test_v49.py:522 class `attribute` (Interpreter().run(reprsweep.PROBE)), is not string-building: it moved the `rest` set 10 -> 11, the third instance of round 488's irreducible module-attribute shape. Its assertion never ran -- the class list sat three lines below `assert len(rows) == 114` in the same function and pytest stops at the first failing assert, so the shape assertion has been unreachable on every corpus addition since round 474, and so was the location pin below it, which round 492's ad7ff7f had made stale (test_v48.py 129 -> 138, 355 -> 373). Fixed in v0.50 / decision 64: size and shape are separate nodes, an AST gate (tests/test_testcorpus_contributions.py::test_the_shape_of_the_residual_is_asserted_where_no_count_can_shadow_it) keeps them apart, and the totals are the sums of state/whence/testcorpus-contributions.json so a corpus addition is one regeneration instead of six re-guessed literals. The subject_scope and evidence declarations above are unchanged and remain correct.
